{{Short description|Derived descent}}
{{citation style|date=February 2015}}

In algebraic geometry, a '''cohomological descent''' is, roughly, a "[[derived category|derived]]" version of a fully faithful descent in the classical [[descent theory]]. This point is made precise by the below: the following are equivalent:<ref>{{harvnb|Conrad|n.d.|loc=Lemma 6.8.}}</ref> in an appropriate setting, given a map ''a'' from a simplicial space ''X'' to a space ''S'', 
*<math>a^*: D^+(S) \to D^+(X)</math> is fully faithful.
*The natural transformation <math>\operatorname{id}_{D^+(S)} \to Ra_* \circ a^*</math> is an isomorphism.
The map ''a'' is then said to be a morphism of cohomological descent.<ref>{{harvnb|Conrad|n.d.|loc=Definition 6.5.}}</ref>

The treatment in [[Séminaire de Géométrie Algébrique du Bois Marie|SGA]] uses a lot of [[topos theory]]. Conrad's notes gives a more down-to-earth exposition.

== See also ==
*[[hypercovering]], of which a cohomological descent is a generalization
